Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-10-01 | AMZN | Hold | +2.3% | +1.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AMZN and maintain existing exposure at the current weight; deploy no new capital at $248.23, which sits mid-range below the 10-day EMA ($249.66), VWMA ($250.77) and 50-day SMA ($256.19), with MACD at -2.490 under its -2.116 signal and RSI at 44.20. If adding, use a stricter ladder than the trader proposed: 5-10% of a standard allocation only on a daily close above $251.83 and the $250.77 VWMA with above-average volume and a narrowing MACD gap, then another 5-10% only above $256.19 with MACD above signal and zero and RSI above 50, preferably after the Q3 print. Cap total adds at +20% of a standard allocation, equalize dollar risk with ATR-based stops, halt adds and trim one-third below $244.30, and cut to no more than half of a standard allocation below $241.22.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate converges on HOLD, but not because the evidence is empty or evenly split. The bull wins the structural and operating argument; the bear wins the current-price and cash-math argument; at $248.23 those two conclusions offset, and the tiebreaker is a near-symmetric payoff with negative momentum.

The operating case is real and not accounting-driven. Q2 2026 revenue was $200.6B, +19.6% year over year and accelerating from +16.6% in Q1; Q2 operating income was $27.5B, +43.2%; operating margin was 13.69%, +226 bp; H1 margin was 13.43%, +181 bp. Core EPS excluding the non-cash private-equity mark was about $2.16 in Q2 (+29%) and $4.09 in H1 (+25%), with SBC flat at roughly 3.0% of revenue and share count up only 0.5% year to date. Q2 operating cash flow was $45.4B (+40%), OCF/NI was 1.19x, cash plus AFS securities was $176.1B, net cash excluding leases was +$29.7B, and interest coverage was 20.9x. The long-term trend is also intact: price is 2.91% above a rising 200-day SMA ($241.22), the 50-day is above the 200-day by about 6.2%, there is no death cross, and recent lows are higher at $244.30, $244.73 and $246.12. That rules out Sell and makes an outright bearish stance difficult.

But the bear's cash-math and timing case governs at the current quote. Operating cash flow is not free cash flow. H1 2026 FCF was -$27.0B, TTM FCF was -$11.6B, and Q2 capex was $54.2B, or 27.0% of revenue. Annualizing that run-rate implies roughly $217B of capex against TTM operating cash flow of $161.4B, a structural deficit now visible in the balance sheet: long-term debt up 93.2% to $133.0B in six months, total debt plus finance leases up 81% to $146.4B, net cash excluding leases down to $29.7B from $51.4B, net debt including operating leases at $66.7B versus $37.9B at year-end, current ratio at 1.03x, and interest expense up 155% to $1.31B, only just offset by $1.30B of interest income. Interest coverage of 20.9x means this is not distress, but the $650B contractual-obligation book should be read as a levered bet on AI demand converting, not as confirmed backlog: the Anthropic >$100B figure comes from a draft prospectus with affordability questioned, the Constellation PPA is a 20-year power agreement with 190 MW arriving 2030-2032, and Synopsys is >$1B over multiple years. Those are directionally bullish, but none is a near-term cash catalyst. At roughly 31x core TTM EPS of $7.9-$8.0, AMZN is fully valued for a negative-FCF, relevering business, even with 19.6% revenue growth and 43% operating-income growth.

Earnings quality is a real overhang but not the deciding one. The $62.8B of non-cash marks on $120.7B of H1 pre-tax income is ugly, and a 10% markdown on the $122.3B model-valued stake is roughly $12.2B pre-tax, or about $1.12 per share, under half a percent of the share price. Core EPS still grew 25-29%, so the operating engine is not being bought with accounting gains. The $38.1B AOCI increase remains unexplained in the provided data and is an open item, not a resolved bull or bear point.

The tape is the immediate tiebreaker. The $248.23 close is below the 10-day EMA at $249.66, VWMA at $250.77 and 50-day SMA at $256.19; MACD at -2.490 is below its -2.116 signal; RSI at 44.20 is weak but not oversold. The October 1 session opened at $251.61, tagged $251.83 and reversed to a $246.12 low, confirming overhead supply at the $250-$252 shelf. Lower highs run from $287.20 to $280.14 to $267.56 to $259.49 to $251.83. Downside to the $241.22 strategic line is about 2.8%, while upside to the $256.19 50-day is about 3.2%: a nearly symmetric payoff with negative momentum, sitting in the middle of the range even the bull says not to chase.

Within the debate, the aggressive analyst is right about the franchise and the opportunity cost of being underexposed, but his ladder is poorly risk-balanced. A first tranche at a close above $251.83 would retest the exact rejection level and still leave AMZN below the 50-day; the proposed second tranche is twice the size while sitting much farther from the $244.30 stop, about 2.10 ATR versus 1.33 ATR for the first. That is not controlled risk-taking. The conservative analyst is right about the rejection level, the gap risk and the need for confirmation, but too absolute in refusing any starter until every condition and the Q3 print are past; the operating record and rising 200-day do not justify treating AMZN as broken. The neutral analyst supplies the correct calibration: keep existing exposure, no new capital at $248.23, cap total adds at +20%, require a volume-backed close above $251.83/VWMA for a small first tranche, require $256.19 with MACD positive and RSI above 50 for a second, and size the second tranche to equal or lower dollar risk.

What would change the call: upgrade toward Overweight or Buy on a volume-confirmed close above $256.19 and then $259.49 with MACD above signal and zero, plus at least one hard fundamental confirmation such as Q3 capex at or below Q2's $54.2B with operating margin at least 13.7%, TTM FCF turning positive, stable-to-lower debt plus leases, or disclosed AWS segment/backlog evidence. Downgrade toward Underweight or Sell on a daily close below $244.30 that fails to reclaim within two to three sessions, a close below $241.22, a material markdown of the $122.3B equity stake, interest expense outrunning interest income, or a capex guide-up paired with decelerating operating cash flow. Data gaps: no portfolio, holdings or cash context, so all sizing is a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation and should be netted against other AI-capex exposure; no sentiment report, options-implied volatility or skew; no AWS segment revenue, margin or verified backlog; no management FCF/capex guidance for the back half; no confirmation status for the Anthropic commitment; and no explanation for the $38.1B AOCI increase.

**Price Target**: 256.19

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored at the Q3 print or on the $244.30 / $256.19 triggers, whichever comes first

REFLECTION:
The +1.0% five-day alpha (+2.3% raw) is too short to judge the 3–6 month Hold thesis, but it tilts against the immediate bearish tape read rather than confirming it. That undercuts the “no new capital at $248.23” timing piece—AMZN outperformed SPY—while leaving the FCF, debt, capex and valuation arguments untested. Next time, predefine a small starter tranche at the first reclaim trigger so a Hold does not become de facto underexposure when near-term alpha turns positive.

[2026-09-30 | AMZN | Hold | +4.3% | +2.4% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Hold

**Executive Summary**: Hold AMZN at a standard 1.0x allocation: do not initiate or add at 249.15, and do not top up anywhere in the 249-256.15 middle, where overhead supply (20-SMA 252.35, VWMA 251.16) and stop-based reward-to-risk of ~1.0-1.25:1 make this a coin flip into the late-October Q3 print. Pre-print, allow at most one small 0.25x boundary probe — a volume-confirmed (>40M) daily close above 256.12 with RSI through 53 and MACD above signal (stop 247.65), or the 239.82-241.60 confluence holding on a closing basis (stop 235.50) — sized so a gap-through costs no more than ~0.3-0.5% of portfolio value, and reserve any move toward 1.25x for post-Q3 confirmation. Execute the downside ladder mechanically: close below 244.30 cuts to 0.6x, close below 241.11 (200-SMA regime change) cuts to 0.3x, and full exit only on a close below 235.50 accompanied by deteriorating Q3 fundamentals. Horizon 1-3 months, re-scored on the Q3 print or the 256.12 / 244.30 triggers.

**Investment Thesis**: The rating is Hold because the seats agree on everything that sizes the position and disagree only where the evidence is genuinely thin. All four voices — aggressive, neutral, conservative, trader — converge on: no initiation at 249.15, no adds in the 249-256.15 middle, maintain the core, and cut on closing breaks of 244.30 and 241.11. That unanimity is the decision; the remaining dispute is how much pre-print optionality to fund, and there the arithmetic and the cash-flow evidence both favor the neutral/conservative construction over the aggressive one.

The aggressive seat loses on quantified reward-to-risk, not on conviction. Its framing of the boundary entries as "asymmetric" was never defended against the identical calculation made independently by the conservative and neutral seats: from 256.15 with the 247.65 stop, risk is 8.50 points against 2.30-4.66 points to the first target zone (258.45-260.81) — roughly 0.27-0.55:1 — and only ~1.34:1 stretching to 267.56. From the current 249.15 against a 240.50 stop and a 258-260 target it is ~1.0-1.25:1. Three seats reached that number; the aggressive seat answered with assertion. The tape read supports the caution rather than the bullish tilt: AMZN closed 249.15 below the 10-EMA (249.982), 2.72% below a rolling-over 50-SMA (256.119, first four-session decline since July) and 0.81% below VWMA (251.161), MACD at -2.496 under its -2.022 signal and below zero since 2026-09-09, RSI 45.20 rejected twice at the 50-53 band, and the 252.44 high that pierced the 20-SMA (252.349) by nine cents closing at 48% of the day's range — a mechanical test-and-fail, and a squeeze that sits below a falling 50-SMA is direction-agnostic, not bullish.

The aggressive seat also loses on cash quality, which is the Research Manager's decisive ground. TTM FCF is -$11.63B versus +$13.48B the prior period; capex is $173B TTM at 26-27% of revenue; $650.03B of contractual obligations with $78.08B due inside twelve months makes capex contracted rather than discretionary, so the FCF bear case and the overbuild bear case are not mutually exclusive; D&A is +32% YoY with a projected $35-55B annual P&L headwind still ahead; long-term debt is $133.0B (+93% in six months) with Q2 interest expense up ~100%; and the $122.3B non-marketable book already absorbed $62.8B of H1 marks ($50.49B in Q2), making core Q2 EPS ~$1.95 versus reported $5.75 — roughly 32x core with negative FCF. None of that is solvency stress, and I reject Sell: revenue of $200.6B (+19.6%, accelerating from +16.6%), operating income of $27.5B (+43.2%) at a 13.7% margin (+230bp), $71.4B of H1 operating cash flow (+44.2%), $176.1B of cash and securities, ~$29.6B of net cash pre-leases and 24x interest coverage mean the business funds the build.

The conservative seat wins pre-print restraint but overcorrects. It is right that stops do not fill through gaps — this name gapped +15.32% on 2026-07-31 with a -9.73% two-day drop in the sample — and right that a ~1.4-ATR box ahead of a binary print is a bet on resolution timing. It is wrong to bar the 239.82-241.60 tranche entirely: the neutral seat correctly showed ~2.6-3.1:1 notional reward to 258-260, and the confluence is triple-stacked (gap floor 239.82 / rising 200-SMA 241.108 / 50% retracement 241.60) with price +3.34% above a rising 200-SMA and 50>200 intact, RSI never breaking 30 through a 12.3% drawdown (higher lows 39.45 -> 41.24 -> 41.93 -> 45.20), MACD histogram higher lows (-1.683 -> -1.539 -> -0.474) against a price lower low, Bollinger bandwidth compressed to 6.71% from 29.58% on 2026-08-19 and ATR to 5.654 (2.27%) from 9.948. Downside is as unproven as upside. The conservative's 0.25x vs 0.3x distinction below the 200-SMA is not the risk driver; gap-risk sizing and total pre-print exposure are.

I therefore adopt the neutral construction and explicitly override the Research Manager's 1.25x/1.5x pre-print allowance: that sizing was justified on a reward-to-risk ratio that did not survive cross-examination. Core stays 1.0x, hard cap 1.0x into the print, one 0.25x boundary probe maximum (not both boundaries), and any path back to 1.25x requires Q3 evidence: revenue ~$205-210B, operating margin >=13% despite D&A, capex/FCF guidance not deteriorating, with the final 0.25x only on a close above 260.81 toward 267.56. Prior AMZN decisions cut both ways and are applied here: the three successive Underweight calls captured -3.7% and -2.1% alpha as price fell from 258.45 to 249.27, so the de-risking has already been delivered and another conviction cut at mid-box, ~3% above a triple-confluence shelf, is not supported; but the 09-16 GOOGL/AAPL lesson that above-spot ladders go unfilled means any future trim must be executed at market, not parked behind 253-256.

What would change the call: upgrade to Overweight on a volume-confirmed close above 256.12 (>40M shares, RSI through 53, MACD above signal) that holds the 50-SMA, plus Q3 capex at or below ~$54.2B with margin >=13.7% and non-deteriorating FCF guidance. Downgrade to Underweight on a daily close below 244.30 that fails to reclaim within two to three sessions, or on any markdown against the $122.3B non-marketable book, a capex guide-up paired with AWS deceleration, or rising D&A guidance paired with a capex/FCF miss. Gaps not papered over: no portfolio/holdings/cost basis/cash, so sizing is a multiple of the caller's standard allocation and must be netted against aggregate AI-capex exposure; no segment-level AWS or advertising figures, so the margin-compounding thesis is unverifiable before Q3; no third-party sensitivity on the $122.3B marks beyond the illustrative 30% haircut (~$37B pre-tax, ~$2.60-2.90/share); capex guidance not broken out by year; no options/implied-volatility or insider data, so cash is the hedge; and no market-moving AMZN-specific disclosure in the supplied news sample.

**Price Target**: 260.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print or on the 256.12 reclaim / 244.30 break triggers, whichever comes first

REFLECTION:
The +4.3% raw / +2.4% alpha over five days says the Hold was directionally wrong-footed — price ran from 249.15 to roughly 260, through the entire 249-256.15 "coin flip" middle — but five sessions against a 1-3 month, Q3-print-anchored thesis is too short to judge the thesis itself; only the pre-print posture got marked.

What this undercuts is the mid-box paralysis: the tape resolved up, not down, and the 0.25x volume-confirmed probe above 256.12 that the plan permitted (but did not pre-commit to) was the trade that paid, while the reward-to-risk arithmetic that killed the 1.25x sizing looks over-fitted to a 1.4-ATR box that broke upward. What it supports is the refusal to cut into the 239.82-241.60 confluence and the mechanical trigger ladder — the framework's conditional logic would have flipped to Overweight correctly had it been executed rather than held as optionality.

Lesson for the next similar setup: when RSI and MACD are printing higher lows against a price lower low and a triple-stacked shelf sits ~3% below, don't call mid-box a coin flip and then hold flat — pre-commit the probe at market on the reclaim trigger and explicitly price in the cost of being flat if it fires.

[2026-09-29 | AMZN | Overweight | +3.9% | +2.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, not the trader's outright Buy: the fundamental direction is settled but the entry is not, so open only 20–25 units of a 120-unit target near 246.67 (and nothing at all if the caller already holds more than ~40–45 units), with the second 20-unit tranche gated on a daily close back above 244.30 on above-average volume after a test of the 241.01–244.24 confluence. Cap total AMZN exposure at 45–50 units ahead of the unmodeled Q3 print, keep 238.50 as the tactical stop but size to a −5.55% gap toward ~233 rather than to that stop, and reserve the final ~50 units for a daily close above 252.64 on >40M shares (ideally above 256.09) or post-earnings confirmation of operating margin ≥13.7% with capex at or below Q2's $54.2B. A daily close below 239.80 cuts tactical adds back to ~40 units, below 235.50 reduce to 25, and any pre-earnings strength into 250.17–252.64 is a trim, not an add.
